accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum in England, Year 2 science (Living things and their habitats: living things live in habitats to which they are suited; name plants and animals in their habitats, including microhabitats) and NGSS 2-LS4-1. Tide facts (two highs and two lows about every 24 h 50 min on most British coasts) match the NOAA tides primer. Each adaptation was checked on MarLIN species pages: common limpet clamps with its foot and returns to a home scar; barnacles close their plates; beadlet anemone retracts tentacles at low tide; common starfish grips with tube feet; shore crab and shanny (common blenny) shelter under rocks and wet seaweed. Seaweed is never called a plant, and the lab says starfish have 5 arms only for the common starfish.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-years ideas about the shore: that a sea anemone is a plant or flower (challenge, mastery m1, kid text), that a starfish is a fish (challenge 'Yes, it lives in the sea' and 'Yes, it can swim fast', mastery m5), that rock pool water is rain or pond water (sort step with frog and goldfish, challenge, m3), that the pool drains dry at low tide (step 1 prediction), that animals on the rocks at low tide are stranded and die (step 5 prediction 'Dry up and die') and that a limpet is washed off by waves (step 4 prediction).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpool draws a side-view rocky shore whose hollow keeps sea water while the child drags the tide level down and up; the sea only fills open air below its level. It then has the child pick animals by their features in that pool, sort salty versus fresh water animals, choose each animal's own grip for a wave (clamp, hide, sticky foot, tube feet, crack) and drag five animals to hide, shut tight or fold into a blob for low tide. None of this tide and adaptation mechanic exists in flagcoast, flagtide or flagseaneed, and the lab_distinct gate stayed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the idea before the text names it: dragging the sea down leaves the hollow full ('Low tide. The sea went out, but sea water stays in the hollow: a rock pool'), choosing 'swims away' for the limpet returns 'A limpet cannot swim. It pulls its shell down hard on the rock', and dropping the anemone in 'Hide under wet seaweed' returns 'An anemone has no shell and cannot run. It pulls its arms in and waits as a jelly blob'. Placed animals stay in their zones, so the three ways to stay wet are visible together.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions hold a tempting wrong answer that the step then disproves: that the hollow is dry when the tide goes out (step 1 shows the pool stay full), that the big wave washes the limpet away (step 4 shows it clamp and stay), and that an anemone on a dry rock dries up and dies (step 5 shows it fold into a blob and wait). The done line repeats the learner's prediction through A.reveal.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions, each with two wrong answers that name their own slip: rain water and pond water for the salty pool, plant and flower for the anemone, 'lives in the sea' and 'can swim' for the starfish, swimming away and letting go for the limpet, draining dry and just sand for the hollow, and taking the crab home or leaving the rock upside down. Every lab step also gives a per-card message, for example 'A frog needs fresh water, like a pond' and 'A crab has no sticky foot. It scuttles under a rock'.

readability.evidence: The kid text reads at FK grade 1.2 and the adult text at 7.8, inside the family limits in validate_lessons. Sentences are short and concrete (A limpet clamps its shell down on the rock.). The young class gives 56 px buttons, one instruction per screen, and long option tiles wrap onto two lines. The adult text uses the precise terms habitat, microhabitat, intertidal zone, adaptation, high and low tide, tube feet, basal disc and home scar.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases, and the explanation stayed under 12% six-word overlap with every lesson, including Coasts & Beaches, Tides, Waves & Currents and What Ocean Animals Need. Every feedback line names the animal and the body part or behaviour that matters.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android-size viewport, touch) in light and dark for all seven steps before and during Show me: the side-view shore fits with six animals spaced in the hollow, wave option tiles wrap long text such as 'holds on with a sticky foot' onto two lines after the first screenshots clipped it, the three low-tide zones fit side by side, and the code cards wrap 'Take a crab home in a bucket'. Every control is a 56 px button under the canvas as well as a canvas target.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate completed every task with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every canvas action has a labelled button ('Tide out', 'Animal 3', 'goldfish: Not in a rock pool', 'The crab hides under a rock', 'barnacle: Shut tight', 'Take a crab home in a bucket: Not good'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback line. Canvas text is dark ink on white or pale tiles, or the theme text colour on the dark wash.
